title: The Barber's Tale of his Sixth Brother

keywords: the barber's tale of his sixth brother
full_text:
The barber concluded the saga of his family with the story of his sixth brother, Shakkashik, who was celebrated for his quick mind:

"My youngest brother, Shakkashik, was once reduced to absolute poverty. Starving and in rags, he knocked upon the door of a magnificent palace in Baghdad belonging to a noble prince of the famous Barmecide clan. The prince, who was renowned for his whimsical humor, invited Shakkashik into his grand dining hall.

'Welcome, friend!' cried the Barmecide prince. 'Wash your hands and partake of my hospitality!' The servants set before them empty porcelain dishes, empty crystal carafes, and silver spoons. The prince took up his spoon, pretended to dip it into an empty bowl, and smacked his lips: 'Taste this superb lentil soup seasoned with fresh coriander! Have you ever tasted anything so delicious?'

Shakkashik, though his stomach was gnawing with hunger, immediately perceived that the prince was testing his wit and manners. Instead of growing angry, Shakkashik joined the game. He dipped his own empty spoon, chewed on thin air, and exclaimed: 'By heavens, my lord, the coriander is roasted to perfection, and the broth is fit for a caliph!'

Next, the host offered an imaginary roast lamb stuffed with pistachios. Shakkashik pretended to tear off a juicy leg, chewed vigorously, and praised the delicate spice. Course after course of nonexistent delicacies were served, followed by phantom honey pastries and imaginary vintage wine from Shiraz.

When the prince offered a fourth imaginary goblet of wine, Shakkashik pretended to drink deeply, swayed in his seat, rolled his eyes, and suddenly slapped the noble prince on the cheek! The prince gasped: 'What means this insolence?' Shakkashik bowed low and pleaded: 'Forgive me, my generous host! The excellence of your vintage was so potent that it intoxicated your humble guest, and he lost his wits!'

The Barmecide prince laughed until tears streamed down his cheeks. Delighted by Shakkashik’s humor, patience, and brilliant adaptability, he ordered a real, sumptuous banquet to be served at once. He clothed my brother in robes of honor and made him the chief steward of his palace for twenty years."
moral: True wit and good humor in the face of misfortune can turn a mockery into a feast of honor.
